prompts.text: What's a decision we made slowly which turned out better because we didn't rush?
We disagree on a purchase while we're in a shop. How should we handle the decision without arguing in public?
Tell me about a time we researched something together and ended up choosing an unexpected option.
People value purchases differently depending on whether they care more about durability, convenience or appearance.
Buy one lasting item for our home or save towards several smaller improvements?
Knowing why someone wants an item matters more than questioning the price first.
Which possession would you repair rather than replace, even if replacement were affordable?
An appliance breaks during a busy week. What would help us decide whether to fix it immediately?
Recall a time we avoided an unnecessary expense and found a better solution.
Browse a bookshop together or choose a book for each other without hints?
What sort of story do you most enjoy hearing someone tell about their life?
People reveal their interests through the questions they ask after a story ends.
We're invited to share a memorable experience at a gathering. Which part would you want to tell?
The person who remembers details isn't always the person best suited to tell the story.
Tell me about a time you heard me describe an event and realised we remembered it differently.
Which book, film or song helped you explain something about yourself?
Listen to a full album together or discuss one lyric which stayed with you?
We watch a film with an ending we interpret differently. What would make the conversation interesting?
Different responses to a character sometimes reflect experiences outside the story itself.
Describe a scene from a film you understood differently after we discussed it.
When have you felt surprised by a creative choice I genuinely enjoyed?
Taste isn't a competition, especially between people who want to understand each other.
Exchange childhood favourite songs or find a new artist neither of us knows?
A friend invites us to a concert featuring music only one of us enjoys. How would you decide together?
Tell me about a song which brings back a particular season of your life.
What's a piece of music you would want playing during an ordinary Sunday at home?
Some songs become markers of shared experiences without anyone choosing them deliberately.
We make a playlist for a road journey. How would you want to divide the choices?
Sing along badly together or sit quietly and focus on the music?
Letting someone enjoy a favourite song without talking over it is an understated kindness.
Which question do you wish people asked more often about your profession or studies?
Tell me about a lesson you learnt from somebody who worked in a different field.
Partners may interpret the word ambitious differently, even when they admire each other's drive.
One of us wants to work fewer hours despite earning less. What questions should we ask before deciding?
Review our weekly plans together on Sunday evening or check in briefly each morning?
What part of your work are you proud of even though others rarely see it?
A job title tells you less about someone than how they approach their responsibilities.
Describe a time you solved a problem at work in a way that surprised you.
You're offered a role with more responsibility but less personal time. What would make the decision worthwhile?
Career success means stability, freedom, learning or recognition depending on the person.
How do you want our home life to change when one of us has a particularly intense period at work?
Leave work conversations outside the bedroom or set aside a short evening check-in?
Tell me about a day you were relieved someone didn't immediately ask about your work.
I forget an important event because I'm concentrating on a deadline. What would meaningful repair look like?
Being busy explains some mistakes but doesn't erase their effect on others.
What sort of reminders feel helpful to you rather than controlling?
Some people express concern by offering reminders when the other person mainly wants confidence.
We're coordinating two important appointments on the same day. How should we make room for both?
Keep a shared noticeboard at home or write reminders in our own notebooks?
Recall an occasion when a carefully planned day worked despite an unexpected delay.
Which small responsibility would you be willing to take on because it matters more to me?
Fairness changes with circumstances rather than always requiring identical effort.
One of us is temporarily unable to do their normal household tasks. How should we reassign them without resentment?
A couple's division of responsibilities often develops from unnoticed habits.
Tell me about something practical you learnt from watching an adult care for their family.
What household task has an unexpectedly calming effect on you?
Tackle the most difficult chore together or split up and finish faster?
A relative offers to help us with a task we usually handle privately. How would you decide whether to accept?
Accepting help without surrendering decision-making is a useful relationship skill.
What's a thoughtful way for us to support an elderly relative while respecting their independence?
Describe a conversation with an older person which changed your perspective on commitment.
Advice from an older generation makes more sense when you understand the circumstances behind it.
A family elder expects us to follow a custom we don't practise. How would you start a respectful conversation?
Record family stories as audio or write down their favourite sayings and memories?
What's one value you hope younger members of your family see in how we behave?
Honouring your upbringing and choosing your own path belong together.
Tell me about a family decision you admire because the people involved handled it with care.
Two relatives seek our support in conflicting situations. What would help us remain fair to both?
Family loyalty sometimes requires asking difficult questions rather than agreeing immediately.
Which cultural celebration would you enjoy learning more about before we attend it?
Join a traditional cooking class or watch artisans explain their work?
Recall a time you appreciated a custom more after understanding its history.
We're invited to a ceremony where neither of us knows the expectations. How would you prepare?
Curiosity and good manners matter more than pretending familiarity with every tradition.
What personal habit from your culture do you wish outsiders understood better?
A shared language doesn't guarantee people attach the same meaning to every expression.
One of us uses a phrase which sounds dismissive to the other. How should we explain the intention and impact?
Learn a few phrases in each other's favourite languages or trade family sayings?
Tell me about a word or expression from your childhood which has no satisfying translation.
What kind of humour helps when we're both nervous about something?
Being able to laugh at a mistake works best when nobody feels singled out.
One of us makes a joke which unintentionally hurts the other. What response would help us recover?
People often use humour to signal closeness but need to learn each other's limits.
Share a ridiculous memory to lighten the mood or put on a comedy we both enjoy?
Recall a harmless mistake of mine which you still find funny.
Which joke between us makes no sense to anyone else?
We run into a person who misunderstands an inside joke. How would you explain without embarrassing anyone?
A joke is less valuable when it makes someone afraid to be sincere.
Affectionate teasing requires careful attention to what the other person finds comfortable.
What quality in our conversations would you want to preserve if we lived apart temporarily?
Exchange short voice notes throughout the week or plan one longer video call?
Tell me about a day when we felt connected despite barely speaking.
A temporary change in our schedules reduces our time together. Which commitment would you want us to keep?
Maintaining a connection through change takes more than counting hours spent together.
Which ordinary promise matters enough for us to protect when life gets complicated?
The most reassuring plans often involve simple things within both people's control.
At the end of a challenging month, we have one free evening. What would make it feel like ours again?
Describe an ordinary conversation with me which you wish you had written down.
Make a shared list of things we're grateful for or exchange private letters once a year?
What's one thing you wish we had asked each other sooner when we began spending time together?
